summary: This version of the playlist app copies the sorted playlist into a LinkedList, then inserts a new song at a chosen position and removes another one by index, printing the playlist after each change so you can see the chain relink.

lines.text: Passing the existing playlist to the LinkedList constructor copies every song across, so you keep the same songs in a structure where each entry holds a reference to the ones before and after it instead of a fixed position.

lines.code: int insertAt = 1; // between Respect and One More Time
lines.text: Because indexes start at 0, index 1 is the second slot in the playlist; naming the position in a variable also makes the printed messages below match exactly what happened.
The two-argument add() puts the song at that position by relinking its neighbours, rather than shifting all the songs after it the way an ArrayList would.
Removing by index returns the song that was taken out, which is why it can be stored and printed; note that the index refers to the list as it stands now, after the insertion.
This earlier sort is why the LinkedList prints in artist order rather than the order the songs were added — the copy inherits whatever order the playlist was left in.
